tested: glenfiddich: the 12's Oloroso and bourbon casks and marrying tuns, 40% ABV (80 proof), the label words Our Original Twelve, the high cut point, the Robbie Dhu spring, the producer's tasting notes, William Grant's dates and his seven sons and two daughters, building from 1886 and the first spirit on Christmas Day 1887, the 12 Sherry Cask Finish in Amontillado casks at 43%, the 15's Solera vat kept at least half full. 5 searches.

the-glenlivet: Double Oak and the order of its oaks, the producer's tasting notes against the record's banana and peach, George Smith's licence of 1824 and the parish claim, the ride to Elgin, Upper Drumin and the move to Minmore after the fire of 1858, the death of 1871 and the youngest son trained for the law, the name claim of 1884, the merger with Glen Grant of 1953, Founder's Reserve and its want of an age statement. 6 searches.

the-macallan: Sherry Oak 12's casks (mostly European oak on the main and American pages, exclusively Oloroso seasoned on the Mexican), its strength by market and the producer's tasting notes, the licence of 1824 by a farmer and schoolteacher, Easter Elchies House and 1700, the wine merchant's purchase and the Macallan-Glenlivet name of 1892, the stake of 1986, the takeover of 1996 and the end of the family's hold. 3 searches.

the-balvenie: DoubleWood's twelve years in American oak and nine months in European oak sherry casks, 43% in the United States and 40% in Britain, the producer's tasting notes, work from early 1892 on Balvenie New House, the first spirit of 1 May 1893 from stills from Lagavulin and Glen Albyn, the demolition of the house (1920 or 1929), DoubleWood of 1993, DoubleWood 17 and Caribbean Cask 14. 5 searches.

aberlour: the casks of the numbered batches against the Oloroso and Pedro Ximenez finish, the Sherry Cask Collection of October 2025, the label words, the batch strengths, the bottle of 1898 and where it was found, the launch of about 1997, what the name means and whether it honours the founder, James Fleming's dates and trade, the hospital his legacy built and its opening of 30 April 1900. 5 searches.

Cards and questions of all five: one right answer each, wrong options of one kind, no length clue (the lint holds the group), keys at positions 0, 2, 1, 3, 2, 1, 3, 0, 1, 2, every explain naming the nearest wrong option. Only the Aberlour found-bottle answer was reworded, for the place of the find. No card id changed.

open: glenfiddich: the high cut point is William Grant's on the 12's page and his son Alec's on the history page; the triangular bottle has no agreed year (1956, 1957, 1961).
the-glenlivet: the 1884 right to the name is the house's account (an agreement among the Speyside distillers, by its archive); one secondary source makes it a court claim by a grandson.
the-macallan: 43% in the United States rests on secondary listings; the record says some markets.
the-balvenie: the cooperage was not searched; the second-hand stills from Lagavulin and Glen Albyn now stand in two accounts and stay told as one account's.
aberlour: 1973 or 1975 for the find; the strength range rests on Wikipedia's batch table and shops; whether the label prints cask strength in any words was not settled.

swaps: aberlour: no swap. The author offered Aberlour 12 Year Old Double Cask should the casks have moved; they have not (the Oloroso and Pedro Ximenez bottling is a separate series), so A'bunadh stands as the plan names it.
the-macallan: no swap. The plan's note offered Double Cask 12; Sherry Oak 12 stands as the bottling that teaches sherry seasoned oak, with Double Cask under others.
No other swap proposed; all five flagships stand as the roster names them.
